_GRADING_: Each Assessment Objective graded A* to G. Bands: A*-A (Excellent), B-C (Good), D-E (Satisfactory), F-G (Limited)

_ASSESSMENT_OBJECTIVES_.AO1: Record - Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions
_ASSESSMENT_OBJECTIVES_.AO2: Explore & Select - Explore and select appropriate resources, media, techniques and processes
_ASSESSMENT_OBJECTIVES_.AO3: Develop - Develop ideas through investigations, demonstrating critical understanding of sources
_ASSESSMENT_OBJECTIVES_.AO4: Present - Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions

quest1.title: The Alchemist's Trial of Color
quest1.rationale:
The Alchemist's Trial of Color

Why it's important:
This quest establishes technical literacy in acrylic painting. Before expression or subject matter can succeed, the artist must understand how paint behaves.

Skills developed:

  • Fundamental brush control
  • Understanding paint application techniques (dry brush, washes, layering, scumbling, glazing, etc.)
  • Intentional mark-making
  • Awareness of paint thickness, opacity, and texture

This acts as the mechanical foundation for all later painting quests.
quest1.description:
Within the Hall of Canvases, the elders demand proof of your versatility.
You must create a single painted sample that demonstrates your command of at least ten distinct acrylic techniques.
Each technique represents a trial—layering like stacked enchantments, dry brushing as light as a rogue's step, washes flowing like elemental magic, and more of your choosing.
requirements: Use one Page to unite all techniques
Demonstrate no fewer than 10 different acrylic painting techniques
Each technique must be clearly visible and intentional

levels.A*-A: Exceptional exploration of 12+ techniques; masterful selection of appropriate applications
levels.B-C: Clear exploration of 10-11 techniques; good selection of techniques
levels.D-E: Basic exploration of 8-9 techniques; limited selection awareness
levels.F-G: Minimal exploration of 7 or fewer techniques; poor selection choices

levels.A*-A: Highly refined composition with intentional, masterful presentation
levels.B-C: Well-presented composition with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Adequate presentation; several unresolved areas
levels.F-G: Poor presentation; little evidence of refinement

quest2.title: Echoes of the Masters
quest2.rationale:
Echoes of the Masters

Why it's important:
Copying masterworks trains your eye to recognize successful visual solutions. This quest teaches you to read a painting like a language and understand how style, composition, and technique work together.

Skills developed:

  • Observation and visual analysis
  • Accurate replication of composition and form
  • Understanding of color harmony and brushwork
  • Building technical confidence through repetition

This prepares you to apply these principles creatively in your own work.
quest2.description:
The Council of Scholars has issued a formidable challenge.
Deep within the archives lie masterpieces forged by artists of great movements: Impressionism, Cubism, Surrealism, and beyond.
You must choose one famed painting from any artistic movement and faithfully replicate it, studying its style, technique, and visual language. Through this trial, you will learn the secrets the Masters once wielded.
requirements: Select one famous painting from a recognized artistic movement
Replicate the artwork's composition, style, and technique as closely as possible
Write a reflection documenting your research: why you chose this movement, what techniques you studied, and what you learned about the master's style

levels.A*-A: Deep, thorough research with sophisticated documentation of movement and artist
levels.B-C: Good research with clear documentation of key elements
levels.D-E: Basic research with limited documentation
levels.F-G: Minimal research with poor or missing documentation

levels.A*-A: Masterful replication showing exceptional exploration of style and technique
levels.B-C: Accurate replication with good technical execution
levels.D-E: Adequate replication with noticeable errors
levels.F-G: Poor replication with major deviations from original

levels.A*-A: Sophisticated understanding demonstrated; clear critical analysis of master's style
levels.B-C: Good understanding with clear analysis of style elements
levels.D-E: Basic understanding with limited analysis
levels.F-G: Poor understanding with no meaningful analysis

quest3.title: The Grand Codex of Art Movements
quest3.rationale:
The Grand Codex of Art Movements

Why it's important:
This quest builds art literacy and helps you understand how visual styles evolve. Knowing the history and visual language of art movements allows you to make more informed creative choices.

Skills developed:

  • Research and visual interpretation
  • Translating theory into imagery
  • Stylistic flexibility
  • Designing clear visual information (poster composition)

It strengthens both your critical thinking and your artistic vocabulary.
quest3.description:
The Archivist seeks a visual codex to preserve the knowledge of art across the ages. You have been chosen to create a powerful poster that brings together four different artistic movements; each recorded as its own illuminated entry.
For every movement, you must gather and display its essential lore: the story of its origins, the names of its most influential artists, the defining characteristics that set it apart, and a hand-drawn illustration that captures its spirit.
requirements: For each of the four artistic movements, your poster must include:
A clear description of the movement.
The names of important artists.
Key characteristics.
A drawing or illustration that represents the movement's style (any media).
Include a brief written analysis explaining how each illustration captures the movement's essence

rubric.overall: The Grand Codex of Art Movements

levels.A*-A: Extensive, well-documented research with sophisticated visual and written records
levels.B-C: Good research with clear documentation of information
levels.D-E: Basic research with incomplete documentation
levels.F-G: Minimal research with sparse or inaccurate records

levels.A*-A: Masterful development of ideas showing deep critical understanding of all four movements
levels.B-C: Clear development showing good understanding of movements
levels.D-E: Partial development with limited understanding
levels.F-G: Poor development with no critical understanding

levels.A*-A: Exceptional poster design; masterful layout and visual communication
levels.B-C: Well-designed poster with clear organization
levels.D-E: Adequate design with some organizational issues
levels.F-G: Poor design; disorganized and difficult to read

quest4.title: Trial of the Masters (Summative)
quest4.rationale:
Trial of the Masters (Summative)

Why it's important:
This quest marks the transition from imitation to creative mastery. You must interpret a movement's visual language rather than copy it, which builds artistic independence.

Skills developed:

  • Creative interpretation and abstraction
  • Applying stylistic elements intentionally
  • Concept development and visual storytelling
  • Advanced composition and color use

This is a summative challenge proving mastery of art concepts.
quest4.description:
The Dark Lord captured the Old Modern Masters and want to reshape visual art to its liking. With your newly acquired skills you are tasked to choose one major art movement and uncover its core visual language.
Through research and experimentation, you will learn the movement's key ideas: how it uses color, form, space, emotion, or abstraction. Then, wield acrylic paint to create an original artwork that reflects those ideas — not a copy, but a creative interpretation worthy of a Master.
requirements: Select one major art movement
Study its key visual ideas and characteristics
Create an original acrylic painting inspired by the movement
Show clear connections between your artwork and the chosen movement
Document your research and development process with sketches and written reflections
Write a final reflection explaining how your artwork interprets the movement's visual language

levels.A*-A: Exceptional research documentation; sophisticated recording of observations and insights
levels.B-C: Good research with clear documentation of ideas
levels.D-E: Basic research with limited recording
levels.F-G: Minimal research with poor documentation

levels.A*-A: Masterful exploration and selection of media and techniques appropriate to the movement
levels.B-C: Good exploration with appropriate selections
levels.D-E: Basic exploration with limited selection awareness
levels.F-G: Poor exploration with inappropriate selections

levels.A*-A: Highly original interpretation demonstrating sophisticated critical understanding
levels.B-C: Clear, original interpretation showing good understanding
levels.D-E: Derivative interpretation with limited understanding
levels.F-G: Copy-like interpretation with no critical understanding

levels.A*-A: Masterful presentation of a highly personal, meaningful response
levels.B-C: Clear personal response with good presentation
levels.D-E: Adequate response with basic presentation
levels.F-G: Weak response with poor presentation

quest5.title: The Geomancer's Trial
quest5.rationale:
The Geomancer's Trial

Why it's important:
Simple shapes force you to focus on value and form without distractions. This is the foundation of realistic painting because it trains your eye to see light and shadow clearly.

Skills developed:

  • Value control (light, midtone, dark)
  • Shading and blending
  • Understanding 3D form
  • Composition through shape placement

Mastering this makes all later subject matter easier.
quest5.description:
The Order of Geomancers tests all aspiring artists in the fundamentals of visual magic.
Your task is to create a painting built from three different shapes, each carefully crafted to show mastery of value (light and dark).
Through deliberate shading, layering, and surface effects, you will give each shape its own presence and depth. Though simple in form, this trial demands close attention to contrast and tactile illusion.
requirements: Include three clearly different shapes
Focus on value using light, mid-tone, and dark areas
Paint all elements in a single cohesive composition
Make sure that there's a smooth transition of colours (blending)

levels.A*-A: Masterful value control; exceptional blending and shading techniques
levels.B-C: Good value control with clear light, mid-tone, dark areas and blending
levels.D-E: Basic value control; blending inconsistent or incomplete
levels.F-G: Poor value control; minimal shading or blending

levels.A*-A: Exceptional craftsmanship; perfectly smooth transitions and clean edges
levels.B-C: Good craftsmanship; smooth transitions and careful execution
levels.D-E: Adequate craftsmanship; some rough transitions or messy areas
levels.F-G: Poor craftsmanship; harsh transitions and careless execution

quest6.title: The Alchemist's Smoothness
quest6.rationale:
The Alchemist's Smoothness

Why it's important:
Blending is one of the most difficult skills in painting. This quest teaches control of pigment, timing, and brush pressure so you can create seamless gradients.

Skills developed:

  • Smooth transitions and gradients
  • Brush pressure control
  • Color mixing and harmony
  • Patience and precision

This skill is essential for skies, skin, soft lighting, and realistic textures.
quest6.description: The Chromatic Guild has summoned you to prove your skill in the mystical art of color blending. Your task is to mix, layer, and transition paints to create a cohesive color scheme, where each color merges smoothly into the next. Precision, patience, and control of pigment are your weapons in this trial.
requirements: Choose a range of colors to blend
Create smooth transitions between each color
Present a finished work where the color progression is clear and harmonious
Remember that paint dries up faster on paper

levels.A*-A: Seamless blending with excellent control and consistent transitions
levels.B-C: Smooth blending with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Blending attempted but transitions are uneven or patchy
levels.F-G: Little evidence of blending technique or control

levels.A*-A: Highly refined composition with intentional choices throughout
levels.B-C: Mostly refined with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Some refinement; several unresolved areas
levels.F-G: Little evidence of refinement

quest7.title: The Woody Grain's Challenge
quest7.rationale:
The Woody Grain's Challenge

Why it's important:
Texture makes surfaces believable. Wood requires controlled irregularity, which trains your eye to observe subtle patterns and replicate them accurately.

Skills developed:

  • Textural linework and pattern
  • Controlled shading for depth
  • Surface variation and realism
  • Attention to detail

It strengthens your ability to depict natural materials and environments.
quest7.description: Wood is struggling with his patterns and needs help. To succeed, you must observe the subtle lines, knots, and grains that make each piece of wood unique, and translate them onto your page with precision and care. This trial will sharpen your skills in texture, line work, and shading as you bring wood to life with your pencil or pen.
requirements: Study a piece of wood or reference image carefully
Draw realistic wood textures, including grain, knots, and natural patterns
Use shading and line work to convey depth and surface quality
Produce a finished drawing that clearly represents wood

levels.A*-A: Wood texture is highly realistic with exceptional control of shading and detail
levels.B-C: Clear wood texture with good shading and accurate patterns
levels.D-E: Texture shown but lacks realism or consistency
levels.F-G: Minimal or inaccurate texture; poor execution

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition; creative interpretation of natural wood patterns
levels.B-C: Good composition; solid representation with intentional choices
levels.D-E: Basic composition; straightforward representation with limited creativity
levels.F-G: Poor composition; no creative interpretation

quest8.title: Bob of the Silver Hall
quest8.rationale:
Bob of the Silver Hall

Why it's important:
Metal surfaces teach you how light behaves on reflective materials. This quest trains your ability to create high contrast, sharp edges, and accurate highlights.

Skills developed:

  • High contrast value control
  • Sharp vs. soft edge handling
  • Reflective logic and highlight placement
  • Precision rendering

This skill is essential for realism and for making objects appear tangible.
quest8.description: The robot Bob of the Silver Hall have summoned you to master the craft of metallic illustration. Your task is to observe how light dances across metal surfaces—gleaming, reflecting, and bending around edges—and render it on your page with careful shading and precision. Through this trial, you will gain the power to make even the coldest metal appear lifelike.
requirements: Study a piece of metal or reference image carefully
Paint realistic metal surfaces, including reflections, highlights, and shadows
Use shading and contrast to convey depth, form, and reflective qualities
Produce a finished drawing that convincingly represents metal

levels.A*-A: Metal surface appears highly realistic with perfect highlight control and reflections
levels.B-C: Metal surface is realistic with good contrast and accurate reflections
levels.D-E: Some metallic qualities shown, but reflections or contrast are weak
levels.F-G: Minimal metallic rendering; surface appears flat

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition; creative approach to depicting reflective surfaces
levels.B-C: Good composition; solid representation with thoughtful choices
levels.D-E: Basic composition; straightforward representation
levels.F-G: Poor composition; no creative consideration

quest9.title: The Alchemist's Gilded Trial
quest9.rationale:
The Alchemist's Gilded Trial

Why it's important:
Gold is a complex color that requires understanding warm/cool shifts and subtle highlights. This quest trains your color intelligence and your ability to render luminous surfaces.

Skills developed:

  • Warm/cool color contrast
  • Subtle value transitions
  • Luminous highlight placement
  • Material realism

It strengthens your ability to paint luxury materials, jewelry, and fantasy details.
quest9.description: The Golden Guild has summoned you to master the art of gilded illustration. Gold is no ordinary metal—it shines, reflects, and radiates light differently than any other surface. Your task is to study its glow, highlights, and subtle color shifts, and render it on your page using careful shading, contrast, and attention to detail. Success in this trial will grant your art the touch of true alchemy.
requirements: Study a piece of gold or reference image carefully
Paint realistic gold surfaces, showing highlights, reflections, and tonal variations
Use shading, contrast, and warm tones to convey its luminosity
Produce a finished painting that convincingly represents gold

levels.A*-A: Gold appears luminous and realistic with perfect warm/cool color shifts and highlights
levels.B-C: Gold appears realistic with good highlights and warm tones
levels.D-E: Gold shown but lacks strong value shifts or convincing highlights
levels.F-G: Minimal evidence of gold rendering; appears flat or incorrect color

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition; creative interpretation of gold's luminous qualities
levels.B-C: Good composition; solid representation with thoughtful highlight placement
levels.D-E: Basic composition; straightforward representation
levels.F-G: Poor composition; no creative consideration

quest10.title: The Verdant Painter's Trial
quest10.rationale:
The Verdant Painter's Trial

Why it's important:
Nature is complex and chaotic, but must be simplified into readable marks. This quest teaches you how to translate organic shapes into paint through texture and layered color.

Skills developed:

  • Layering and brushstroke variation
  • Atmospheric depth
  • Organic form and movement
  • Color variation in nature

This is essential for landscapes and environmental painting.
quest10.description: The Wardens of the Green Realm call upon you to study the living language of nature. Trees and grass are ever-changing—shaped by wind, light, and growth. Your task is to observe their forms, colors, and textures, then translate them into paint using layered strokes, value, and color variation. Through this trial, you will bring the landscape to life on your canvas.
requirements: Paint trees and grass within a single composition
Show texture through brushstrokes and layering
Use value and color variation to create depth and form
Demonstrate natural movement and organic shapes

levels.A*-A: Strong layered texture and depth; masterful brushwork; clear movement and organic form
levels.B-C: Good texture and depth with minor inconsistencies; solid brushwork
levels.D-E: Some texture but depth or form is weak; limited brush variation
levels.F-G: Minimal layering or texture; flat appearance; poor brushwork

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition; creative interpretation of natural forms and atmosphere
levels.B-C: Good composition; solid representation with thoughtful color choices
levels.D-E: Basic composition; straightforward representation of nature
levels.F-G: Poor composition; no creative interpretation of landscape

quest11.title: Duel of the Silent Master (Summative)
quest11.rationale:
Duel of the Silent Master (Summative)

Why it's important:
Still life is the ultimate test of observation. This quest forces you to practice accurate proportion, value, and material rendering under real-world conditions.

Skills developed:

  • Accurate proportion and form
  • Value hierarchy and shading
  • Surface texture and detail
  • Composition and visual balance

Completing this proves readiness for advanced realistic work.
quest11.description:
Within the Grand Arena of Art stands the reigning Most Valuable Painter, a master known for turning simple objects into legendary works. You have been summoned to challenge this champion — not with blades, but with brush and sight.
Before you lies a still life assortment of items: silent, unmoving, yet demanding absolute focus. To defeat the MVP, you must outmatch them in observation, composition, and control of paint. Every shadow must be earned. Every highlight must strike true.
requirements: Study the still life with unwavering focus
Paint the objects with accurate proportion and form
Use value and shading to create depth and realism
Capture surface textures convincingly
Arrange and paint the scene with balance and intention
Write a reflection explaining your observational process, challenges faced, and how you achieved realism

rubric.overall: Duel of the Silent Master (Portfolio Piece)

levels.A*-A: Excellent documentation of observational process and reflections on challenges
levels.B-C: Good documentation with clear explanation of process
levels.D-E: Basic documentation with limited reflection
levels.F-G: Minimal or missing documentation

levels.A*-A: Outstanding realism with excellent control of value, texture, and technique
levels.B-C: Strong realism with minor technical flaws
levels.D-E: Some realism but inconsistencies in value or form
levels.F-G: Poor technical execution

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition; creative arrangement of still life elements showing developed understanding
levels.B-C: Good composition with thoughtful arrangement
levels.D-E: Basic composition; straightforward arrangement
levels.F-G: Poor composition; no intentional arrangement

levels.A*-A: Masterful presentation of a highly refined still life
levels.B-C: Good presentation with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Adequate presentation with some unresolved areas
levels.F-G: Poor presentation with little evidence of refinement

quest13.title: The Sigils of Order
quest13.rationale:
The Sigils of Order

Why it's important:
Patterns teach control, repetition, and rhythm. This quest builds your ability to create visually coherent artwork through intentional mark-making.

Skills developed:

  • Repetition and variation
  • Visual consistency
  • Abstract composition
  • Control over line and shape

This strengthens design skills and visual discipline.
quest13.description: Ancient scribes once controlled chaos through repeated marks and symbols. Now this knowledge should be passed to you. You must design an abstract work built from repetition, variation, and rhythmical order. Pattern may be strict or evolving—but it must command the surface.
requirements: Use repetition of shapes, lines, or marks
Show variation within the pattern
Avoid representational imagery
Create visual consistency across the artwork
Use colours

levels.A*-A: Pattern is highly controlled, balanced, and intentional
levels.B-C: Pattern is clear and consistent with minor flaws
levels.D-E: Pattern shows some control but lacks consistency
levels.F-G: Pattern is inconsistent or unclear

levels.A*-A: Exceptional composition with strong visual rhythm and creative variation
levels.B-C: Good composition with effective variation
levels.D-E: Basic composition with limited variation
levels.F-G: Unorganized or chaotic composition

quest14.title: The Skilled Blacksmith
quest14.rationale:
The Skilled Blacksmith

Why it's important:
Emphasis is a core visual skill. This quest trains you to control viewer focus using contrast, scale, color, and detail.

Skills developed:

  • Focal point creation
  • Contrast and hierarchy
  • Composition through value and color
  • Abstract storytelling

This is essential for creating strong visual impact in any art style.
quest14.description: The blacksmith Kyrgsth creates one-of-a-kind weapons, and he is looking for someone to pass on his technique. Your task is to create an abstract composition where one area clearly dominates through contrast, scale, color, or detail—while the rest supports it.
requirements: Use contrast (value, color, size, or texture)
Keep the artwork non-representational
Ensure supporting areas enhance the focal point

levels.A*-A: Contrast is used masterfully with strong visual hierarchy
levels.B-C: Contrast is effective with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Contrast is present but inconsistent
levels.F-G: Little to no effective contrast

levels.A*-A: Focal point is extremely strong and clearly dominant; creative use of contrast
levels.B-C: Focal point is strong and clear
levels.D-E: Focal point is present but weak or unclear
levels.F-G: No clear focal point

quest15.title: The Pulse of Rhythm
quest15.rationale:
The Pulse of Rhythm

Why it's important:
Movement in art is created through rhythm and repetition. This quest teaches you to guide the viewer's eye through visual beats without relying on recognizable forms.

Skills developed:

  • Visual tempo and flow
  • Repetition with variation
  • Dynamic composition
  • Non-representational design

It strengthens your ability to create energy and motion in static images.
quest15.description: The Dancers of the Visual Realm believe art can move without motion. Even when static, it looks like they are moving. Learn their technique of the static motion so you can do the same. You must create a non-representational composition that feels alive through repeating elements, flowing transitions, or visual beats.
requirements: Use repetition to suggest movement
Create a sense of visual tempo or flow
Avoid recognizable imagery
Guide the viewer's eye across the artwork
Don't mix rhythm and pattern: rhythm uses patterns, but they are not the same thing

levels.A*-A: Repetition and variation used skillfully to suggest motion
levels.B-C: Repetition and variation used effectively with minor flaws
levels.D-E: Some repetition but little variation or motion
levels.F-G: Little evidence of repetition or motion

levels.A*-A: Composition has strong rhythm and clear visual flow; highly creative
levels.B-C: Good rhythm with minor inconsistencies
levels.D-E: Some rhythm but flow is weak or inconsistent
levels.F-G: No clear rhythm or flow

quest19.title: The Beastbinder's Study of Fur
quest19.rationale:
The Beastbinder's Study of Fur

Why it's important:
Painting fur requires patience, observation, and control. This assessment challenges artists to slow down, study texture, and translate subtle variations in value, direction, and layering into believable surface detail.

Skills developed:

  • Layering and brush control
  • Observation of texture and direction
  • Value shifts and color variation
  • Refinement through revision
quest19.description:
In the archives of the Beastbinders, no creature is judged by shape alone.
Its fur tells the true story.
You must create a painted study focused entirely on rendering fur—real or imagined. Through careful layering, directional strokes, and intentional color shifts, you will bring texture and life to the surface of your work.
requirements: Create a painted study focused on fur texture
Use layering and directional brushstrokes to suggest depth and movement
Show intentional variation in value and color
Revise the work based on observation and reflection
Write a brief reflection explaining your layering process and how you achieved texture

levels.A*-A: Excellent reflection explaining layering process and texture techniques
levels.B-C: Good reflection with clear explanation of process
levels.D-E: Basic reflection with limited explanation
levels.F-G: Minimal or missing reflection

levels.A*-A: Exceptional control of layered techniques resulting in highly realistic or expressive fur texture
levels.B-C: Clear and effective use of layering and brushwork to represent fur
levels.D-E: Some attempt at layering; texture appears inconsistent or flat
levels.F-G: Minimal technique use; fur texture not convincingly represented

quest33.title: The Trial of the Blurred Light
quest33.rationale:
The Trial of the Blurred Light

Why it's important:
Bokeh is a key technique for creating depth, atmosphere, and cinematic lighting. This quest teaches edge control and layering to simulate soft focus.

Skills developed:

  • Bokeh effect and soft edge control
  • Layered transparency and glow
  • Depth through overlap and blur
  • Atmospheric lighting

This skill improves mood, depth, and lighting in all future work.
quest33.description:
The Luminary Circle teaches that not all light is sharp—some light whispers. Your task is to create an artwork inspired by the bokeh effect, where light dissolves into soft circles, gentle overlaps, and atmospheric glow.
Through careful layering, blending, and control of edges, you will suggest depth and distance, allowing lights to float and fade as if seen through an unfocused lens.
requirements: Create soft, circular light forms
Use blending and layering to soften edges
Show overlapping shapes to suggest depth
Use color and value to create a glowing effect
Avoid sharp outlines or detailed imagery

rubric.overall: The Trial of the Blurred Light

levels.A*-A: Soft focus is excellent with smooth edges and layered depth
levels.B-C: Soft focus is clear with minor edge issues
levels.D-E: Soft focus is attempted but inconsistent
levels.F-G: Little evidence of soft focus or layering

levels.A*-A: Strong atmospheric interpretation and depth; creative use of glow and overlap
levels.B-C: Good atmospheric effect with minor issues
levels.D-E: Some atmosphere but shallow depth
levels.F-G: No atmospheric effect

quest34.title: Trial of Textured Cubes
quest34.rationale:
Trial of Textured Cubes

Why it's important:
Texture is best learned through simple forms. Cubes isolate texture so you can focus on surface quality without complex anatomy.

Skills developed:

  • Material texture rendering
  • Consistent lighting across surfaces
  • Brushwork variation
  • Form clarity and edge control

This builds the foundation for realistic object rendering.
quest34.description: In this quest, you will explore texture by painting a set of cubes. Each cube must represent a different surface, focusing on how paint application can suggest material.
requirements: Paint/draw at least 4 cubes
Each cube must show a different texture
Use acrylic paint only
Textures must be visually distinct

levels.A*-A: Each texture is distinct and highly convincing
levels.B-C: Most textures are clear and distinct
levels.D-E: Some textures are unclear or repeated
levels.F-G: Textures are not distinct or convincing

levels.A*-A: Lighting and form are highly consistent and refined; creative texture choices
levels.B-C: Lighting is consistent with minor issues
levels.D-E: Lighting is inconsistent or unclear
levels.F-G: Little evidence of lighting or form

quest35.title: The Beast of the Borderlands
quest35.rationale:
The Beast of the Borderlands

Why it's important:
Animal painting combines anatomy, texture, and gesture. This quest teaches you how to create believable forms through observation and structure.

Skills developed:

  • Animal anatomy and proportion
  • Texture rendering (fur, scales, feathers)
  • Gesture and form
  • Expressive character design

This strengthens both realism and imaginative creature design.
quest35.description:
Villagers near the borderlands report sightings of a powerful creature whose presence has unsettled the land. You are asked to document the beast through paint, capturing its form and spirit so the elders may understand it.
Your brush must reveal the animal's strength, texture, and character.
requirements: Paint one animal of your choice
Use acrylic paint
Show clear form and proportions
Include texture such as fur, scales, or feathers

levels.A*-A: Animal anatomy and texture are highly convincing and detailed
levels.B-C: Anatomy and texture are accurate with minor issues
levels.D-E: Some accuracy but anatomy or texture is weak
levels.F-G: Poor anatomy and texture

levels.A*-A: Strong sense of gesture, form, and character; creative interpretation
levels.B-C: Good sense of gesture with minor errors
levels.D-E: Some gesture but lacks clarity
levels.F-G: No clear gesture or character

quest36.title: Chaos Sealed in Color
quest36.rationale:
Chaos Sealed in Color

Why it's important:
Abstract art trains emotional expression and visual decision-making. This quest teaches you to use color and composition intentionally without relying on recognizable objects.

Skills developed:

  • Color harmony and contrast
  • Composition through shape and balance
  • Emotional expression through abstraction
  • Controlled visual tension

This develops your ability to communicate mood and energy.
quest36.description:
A rogue force of chaos has leaked into the realm, twisting balance and order. The Guild believes this energy can be contained through abstraction.
You must create a painting that traps raw emotion, movement, and power without relying on recognizable forms.
requirements: Create a fully abstract acrylic painting
Do not include recognizable objects
Use color intentionally
Create visual balance or tension

levels.A*-A: Strong color harmony and tension with intentional composition
levels.B-C: Good color use with minor compositional issues
levels.D-E: Some color use but composition is weak
levels.F-G: Little intentional color or composition

levels.A*-A: Composition is balanced and powerful, with clear visual intent; highly creative abstraction
levels.B-C: Composition is balanced with minor issues
levels.D-E: Composition shows some balance but is inconsistent
levels.F-G: Composition is disorganized

quest37.title: The Alchemist's Spill
quest37.rationale:
The Alchemist's Spill

Why it's important:
Fluid art teaches you to collaborate with chance while maintaining composition. This quest trains you to guide paint flow while still creating a complete image.

Skills developed:

  • Fluid acrylic control
  • Compositional awareness
  • Color mixing through movement
  • Working with randomness intentionally

This improves spontaneity and creative problem-solving.
quest37.description:
A couple of alchemist's experiment has gone awry, spilling enchanted pigments across the workshop. Instead of cleaning the mess, you are asked to study it.
By guiding the flow of paint, you will uncover hidden patterns within the chaos.
requirements: Create an acrylic pour painting
Use fluid acrylic techniques

He presses a worn sketch into your hands: a quick drawing he made that night, decades ago, from memory. 'This is all I have. But you... you're a painter. You understand light and shadow. I need you to prove you understand this, not by painting the Kraken, but by painting anything, but paint it in the language of the deep. Only value. Only light and shadow. Show me you see the world the way the Kraken does.'

quest74.title: The Serene Brush of the Eastern Masters
quest74.rationale:
The Serene Brush of the Eastern Masters

Why it's important:
Traditional Chinese painting is not about replication, but about capturing the 'spirit' or 'essence' (Qi) of a subject with the fewest, most deliberate strokes. This quest introduces a completely different philosophical approach to art, emphasizing fluidity, control, and harmony with nature.

Skills developed:

  • Mastery of ink wash and brush control on absorbent paper
  • Understanding of calligraphic line quality and its expressive power
  • Compositional principles of negative space (留白, liú bái) and balance

This quest expands your artistic vocabulary beyond Western techniques, teaching you a meditative and highly disciplined approach to image-making.

You must learn to paint not what you see, but what you feel: the bamboo's resilience, the bird's fleeting life, the mountain's eternal silence. Using only ink/watercolour, water, and a brush, you must create a composition that embodies the principles of harmony, balance, and spiritual essence.
requirements: Research and select a traditional Chinese painting subject

quest72.title: The Scroll of Unwritten Fates
quest72.rationale:
The Scroll of Unwritten Fates

Why it's important:
This summative quest combines narrative storytelling, character design, and sequential art—the core pillars of manga creation. Creating a complete comic requires students to integrate multiple artistic skills while managing pacing, composition, and visual flow across pages. The 10-page constraint teaches economy of storytelling, forcing focused narrative development and intentional panel design.

Skills developed:

  • Sequential storytelling and narrative pacing
  • Character design and visual consistency
  • Panel composition and page layout
  • Inking and toning techniques
  • Visual communication of emotion and action

This quest demonstrates mastery of comic art fundamentals while encouraging creative writing and visual problem-solving.
quest72.description:
In the Silent Library of Kyō, there exists an ancient scroll that remains perpetually blank—the Scroll of Unwritten Fates. Its keeper, the archivist Kumo, explains its curse: it absorbs stories but erases them instantly unless rendered with perfect visual conviction.

A shadow creature called Kurayami now feeds on these lost narratives, growing stronger with each forgotten tale. To defeat it, you must create a manga that the scroll cannot consume—a story so visually compelling, so perfectly paced, and so emotionally resonant that it becomes permanent.

Your challenge: Create a 10-page manga comic with a complete narrative arc. Each page must serve the story; each panel must advance character or plot. Through careful composition, expressive characters, and controlled pacing, you will forge a story that withstands the scroll's hunger and banishes Kurayami back to the void between panels.
requirements: Create a complete manga comic (no more than 10 pages)
Include at least 10 panels total across all pages
Feature original characters and story (no fan fiction)
Use proper manga formatting: right-to-left reading, panel gutters, speech bubbles

quest73.title: The Path of the Endless Line
quest73.rationale:
The Path of the Endless Line

Why it's important:
This formative quest introduces the foundational power of line in drawing. By focusing on a single, unbroken line, you learn to see drawing as a continuous, flowing movement rather than a series of disconnected marks. This builds confidence and control.

Skills developed:

  • Hand-eye coordination and fluidity
  • Controlling line weight through pressure
  • Creating complex compositions from a simple element
  • Understanding line as both contour and form
  • Building muscle memory for confident mark-making

This quest acts as a stepping stone to the more complex summative version, allowing for experimentation and risk-taking without the pressure of a final grade.
quest73.description: The Order of Wayfinders teaches that every journey begins with a single line. Before you embark on your epic quest, you must first practice the basics. Your task is to create a one-line drawing. Let your pen or pencil glide across the page without lifting it. It may twist, loop, overlap, or change thickness, but it must be continuous. The goal is not to draw an object, but to explore the expressive potential of a single, endless line.
requirements: Use a single, continuous line without lifting your drawing tool

quest75.title: The Fashionista's Sketchbook
quest75.rationale:
The Fashionista's Sketchbook

Why it's important:
This summative quest bridges figure drawing, textile rendering, and conceptual design. Students must synthesize research, technical drawing skills, and creative vision to produce a cohesive fashion collection. The croquis format emphasizes proportion and movement while allowing for stylized expression. This quest prepares students for design fields and strengthens their ability to present cohesive visual ideas.

Skills developed:

  • Figure drawing proportion and gesture
  • Fabric rendering techniques (texture, folds, sheen)
  • Color theory and palette development
  • Research integration and mood board creation
  • Professional presentation and annotation

This quest demonstrates mastery of observational drawing applied to imaginative, functional design.
quest75.description:
In the bustling atelier of Maison d'Art, the renowned designer Coco has grown weary of fast fashion. She seeks a visionary who can breathe soul back into clothing—someone who understands that garments tell stories before they ever touch fabric.

She hands you a blank sketchbook and a challenge: 'Research a forgotten era or distant culture. Let its spirit move through you. Then, design a mini collection of three original outfits that honor that inspiration while speaking to the future.'

Include color in all three designs
Annotate each design with notes on materials, inspiration, and construction details
Present all three designs as a cohesive mini collection

quest78.title: The Mirror of the Soul-Eater
quest78.rationale:
The Mirror of the Soul-Eater

Why it's important:
Portraiture is the ultimate test of observation, proportion, and value control in drawing. This summative quest challenges students to synthesize all previous sketching skills—facial anatomy, proportion, shading, expression, and texture—into a single cohesive work. Working in pencil or charcoal requires patience, precision, and the ability to see subtle value shifts that bring a face to life. Mastering portraiture builds confidence for all future figurative work.

Skills developed:

  • Accurate facial proportion and feature placement
  • Value control and smooth shading transitions
  • Capturing likeness and expression
  • Rendering skin texture and subtle forms
  • Understanding light logic on complex forms
  • Patience and refinement through revision

This quest demonstrates mastery of observational drawing and the ability to capture human presence and emotion on paper.
quest78.description:
In the forgotten village of Greyhollow, the people have stopped recognizing each other. A mother passes her child on the street and sees a stranger. Friends meet and cannot remember each other's names. The cause is Morwen, the Soul-Eater - a creature that feeds on identity itself, leaving its victims alive but hollow, their faces familiar yet somehow blank.

Morwen cannot steal what is captured in art. A drawing holds the soul still, keeps it safe. But the drawing must be true: every shadow, every curve, every light in the eye. Only a true portrait can defeat it.
requirements: Select a real person as your subject (may be yourself, a classmate, family member, or use a clear reference photo)
Create a portrait drawing in pencil or charcoal showing head and shoulders
Demonstrate accurate facial proportions and feature placement

Render smooth transitions to suggest skin texture and form
Capture the subject's likeness and expression
Write a reflection explaining your process, challenges, and how you captured likeness

quest79.title: The Beast of Thornhollow
quest79.rationale:
The Beast of Thornhollow

Why it's important:
Animal drawing combines anatomical understanding, texture rendering, and gesture observation. Unlike portraits, animals require understanding of different skeletal structures, fur or scale patterns, and the way four-legged creatures move and hold weight. This summative quest challenges students to apply observational skills to a living creature, capturing not just its form but its character and spirit. Mastery of animal drawing prepares students for wildlife art, creature design, and advanced figurative work.

Skills developed:

  • Animal anatomy and proportion
  • Fur, feather, or scale texture rendering
  • Capturing gesture and movement
  • Understanding light on complex forms
  • Creating presence and personality
  • Value control for form definition

This quest demonstrates mastery of observational drawing applied to the animal form and the ability to capture the essence of a living creature.
quest79.description:
Deep in the Thornhollow forest, something moves between the ancient pines. The woodcutters speak of a creature that appears at twilight: massive, silent, watching. They call it the Thornhollow Beast, and they fear it. But the old hunter Kael, who has lived in these woods for eighty winters, knows the truth.

'It's not a monster,' he tells you, stirring his fire. 'It's the last of its kind. I've seen it twice in my life. Each time, it looked at me like it was asking a question. Now it's old. The younger hunters want to track it, kill it, hang its head on a wall.'

Kael's eyes meet yours. 'But you... you carry a sketchbook, not a spear. I need you to find the Beast and draw it. Not a hunter's trophy, a true drawing. Show why it deserves to live. The Beast of Thornhollow isn't a monster. It's a memory made of fur and bone, and memories deserve respect.'

The Face Stealer

quest54.title: The Necklace of the Desert Moon

The Necklace of the Desert Moon

quest58.title: The Citadel of Forms

quest62.title: The Dance of the Wind
quest62.rationale:
The Dance of the Wind

Why it's important:
Movement in sculpture brings life and energy. This quest teaches you how to suggest motion through shape, line, and rhythm in 3D.

Skills developed:

  • Dynamic composition and flow
  • Gesture and rhythm in form
  • Working with curves and directional lines
  • Balance and stability in dynamic shapes
  • Creating movement that reads from multiple angles

This quest builds your ability to create sculptures that feel alive and fluid.
quest62.description:
A wind spirit wants to be seen in solid form. You must create a sculpture that suggests movement—flowing lines, twisting shapes, or dynamic poses.
The piece should feel alive, as if it could shift with the breeze.
requirements: Create a sculpture that suggests movement
Use flowing lines or dynamic shapes
Show direction and rhythm
Make the movement clear from different angles
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board
Write a reflection explaining how you created movement

quest63.title: The Echoing Repetition
quest63.rationale:
The Echoing Repetition

Why it's important:
Repetition creates rhythm and harmony in sculpture. This quest teaches pattern, structure, and consistency while building visual movement.

Skills developed:

  • Pattern creation and repetition
  • Visual rhythm and flow
  • Consistency in repeated forms
  • Balancing repetition with variety
  • Creating sculptural unity through repeated elements

This quest strengthens your ability to create cohesive sculptures with strong visual rhythm.
quest63.description:
A bard of stone wants to hear rhythm through form. You must create a sculpture that uses repetition and pattern to create visual rhythm.
The piece should feel like a repeated beat or pulse, guiding the viewer through its shapes.

quest68.title: The Master Forgemaster's Covenant
quest68.rationale:
The Master Forgemaster's Covenant

Why it's important:
This summative team quest challenges artists to collaborate in designing and constructing a cosplay build using EVA foam. By working in small teams, students must communicate ideas, divide responsibilities, and refine a shared vision while demonstrating craftsmanship and technical growth.

Skills developed:

  • Collaborative planning and problem-solving
  • Experimentation with materials and techniques
  • Three-dimensional construction and craftsmanship
  • Revision, refinement, and process documentation

This quest demonstrates mastery of collaborative design and EVA foam construction.
quest68.description:
No great armor is forged alone.
In this final trial, a small guild of artisans must work together to design and construct a cosplay build using EVA foam. Teams of no more than three must coordinate planning, fabrication, and refinement to produce a cohesive final piece.
requirements: Work in a team of no more than three students
Collaboratively design a cosplay build using sketches or patterns
Experiment with EVA foam techniques during construction
Construct a complete and cohesive cosplay element or set
Refine the final work based on testing, feedback, and team reflection
Document the process, including individual contributions
Write a team reflection explaining collaboration, challenges, and how work was divided

quest70.title: The Animist's Awakening
quest70.rationale:
The Animist's Awakening

Why it's important:
This summative quest bridges functional design with artistic expression. Redesigning an everyday object teaches students to analyze form, function, and aesthetics while developing creative problem-solving skills. The challenge requires both technical 3D construction and conceptual thinking about how objects 'live' in our world.

Skills developed:

  • Analytical observation of existing objects
  • Conceptual redesign and creative transformation
  • 3D construction with mixed media
  • Functional and aesthetic balance
  • Process documentation from research to final product

This quest prepares students for design thinking and encourages them to see the artistic potential in everyday items.
quest70.description:
In the Workshop of Awakened Forms, the old tinkerer Móðir sits surrounded by mundane objects she calls 'sleeping spirits.' She believes every manufactured thing holds a latent personality, waiting to be revealed through redesign.

She hands you an ordinary, mass-produced object—a chair, lamp, table, or similar. 'This one,' she whispers, 'dreams of being more than it is. It yearns for a second life, a truer form.'

Your task is to listen to the object's hidden character and redesign it into something that expresses its soul. You must respect its original function while transforming its appearance, materiality, and presence entirely. The final piece should feel like the object has awakened, revealing what it was always meant to be.
requirements: Select one ordinary, mass-produced object as your starting point
Research and analyze its current form, function, and manufacturing
Create a completely redesigned version that maintains its core function
Use mixed media (clay, wire, found objects, EVA foam, etc.) for construction
Include a written statement explaining your redesign concept
Document your entire process: research → sketches → prototypes → final piece
Write a reflection analyzing your transformation choices

quest71.title: The Dreamweaver's Gambit
quest71.rationale:
The Dreamweaver's Gambit

Why it's important:
This quest combines art history, technical craft, and conceptual translation. Needle felting requires patience, precision, and spatial thinking while reproducing a 2D painting in 3D wool teaches students to analyze color, composition, and texture in new dimensions. The challenge of translating brushstrokes into wool fibers develops both observational skills and material mastery.

Skills developed:

  • Art historical analysis and interpretation
  • Needle felting technique and wool manipulation
  • Color theory application with fiber materials
  • Spatial translation from 2D to 3D form
  • Patience and precision in craft execution

This quest demonstrates how traditional crafts can reinterpret fine art, bridging historical and contemporary making practices.
quest71.description:
The village of Stillaheim is haunted by Mara, the Nightmare Weaver—a creature who traps minds in restless sleep by unraveling their memories into tangled wool. Her power grows from stolen dreams, which she hangs as spectral tapestries in her lair.

Only one art can counter her: the ancient craft of felting, which binds loose fibers into solid truth. The elders have discovered Mara's weakness—she cannot bear to see dreams made permanent, rendered with such conviction that they cannot be undone.

You are tasked with selecting a famous painting whose emotional power matches Mara's dark artistry. Through needle felting, you must recreate this masterpiece in wool, stitch by meticulous stitch. Your felted reproduction must capture not just the image, but the painting's soul—its color harmonies, its emotional weight, its very essence made tangible. Only a work of such crafted truth can unravel Mara's nightmares and restore peaceful sleep.
requirements: Select one famous painting from any art movement or period
Research the painting's composition, color palette, and emotional impact
Create a needle-felted reproduction using wool fibers
Include a color study showing your wool color selections matching the original
Present both the original painting reference and your 3D felted version
Write a brief analysis explaining your translation choices from paint to wool

quest76.title: The Sculptor's Menagerie
quest76.rationale:
The Sculptor's Menagerie

Why it's important:
This summative quest introduces students to figurative sculpture through imaginative creature design. By working with air-dry clay over wire armature, students learn essential 3D construction principles: structural support, additive/subtractive techniques, surface texturing, and spatial thinking. The fantastical subject matter encourages creative risk-taking while still demanding anatomical believability and technical craftsmanship.

Skills developed:

  • Armature construction for structural stability
  • 3D form building and proportion
  • Surface texturing techniques (fur, scales, skin)
  • Understanding balance and weight distribution
  • Creative anatomy and creature design

This quest builds confidence in sculptural practice and prepares students for more complex figurative work.
quest76.description:
Deep in the Whispering Woods, the last Keeper of the Menagerie tends to creatures that exist only in dreams and stories. But the Keeper is aging, and their magic is fading. Soon, these fantastical beasts will be forgotten unless someone can preserve them in solid form.

You have been summoned to the Keeper's workshop, where sketches of impossible creatures line the walls—griffins with feathered serpents' tails, foxes with crystalline antlers, turtles with moss-grown shells. Your task is to choose one creature from the Keeper's sketches—or imagine your own—and bring it to life as a small sculpture.

Using wire to build its hidden skeleton and clay to give it flesh and texture, you must create a creature so convincing that it could almost breathe. The Keeper will know you have succeeded when your sculpture feels balanced, textured, and alive—a permanent guardian for the fading menagerie.
requirements: Design an original fantastical creature or select one from provided references
Create a wire armature that supports the creature's pose and weight
Build the form using air-dry clay, showing clear anatomical understanding
Apply surface textures that suggest fur, scales, feathers, or skin
Ensure the sculpture is structurally stable and balanced
Document your process with photos showing armature, construction stages, and final piece
Include a brief artist statement explaining your creature's inspiration and design choices

quest77.title: The Weaver's Legacy
quest77.rationale:
The Weaver's Legacy

Why it's important:
This culminating quest challenges students to bridge 2D design and 3D construction by creating a wearable piece of art. Students must synthesize figure drawing, textile understanding, and sculptural thinking to transform a flat design into a three-dimensional garment. The process requires planning, problem-solving, and craftsmanship while allowing for immense creative expression. This quest prepares students for costume design, fashion construction, and wearable art practices.

Skills developed:

  • Translating 2D designs into 3D forms
  • Pattern making and construction techniques
  • Material selection and textile manipulation
  • Wearable structure and fit considerations
  • Integrated design process from concept to finished piece

This quest demonstrates mastery of the full design cycle and the ability to bring imagined clothing into physical reality.
quest77.description:
In the mountain loom-halls of the Weaver's Guild, an ancient tradition continues: each year, apprentices must create a single garment that tells a story. Not just any story—a story woven, stitched, and shaped into fabric that can be worn.

The Guild Master, an elderly woman named Elara who has woven garments for queens and kings, has chosen you for the final test. She places before you sketches from throughout history: a warrior's cloak, a dancer's dress, a scholar's robe. 'Choose your inspiration,' she says, 'but do not copy. Listen to what the fabric wants to become.'

Your task is to create an original piece of clothing—a garment that can be worn, displayed on a form, or hung as sculpture. It must begin with the design skills you demonstrated in your fashion sketchbook, showing thoughtful development from 2D concept to 3D reality. Through fabric, stitching, and structure, you will weave your own legacy into the Guild's collection.

Create detailed construction plans including pattern pieces and material lists
Construct a wearable garment or garment equivalent
Demonstrate understanding of fit, structure, and material behavior

Present the finished garment on a form, mannequin, or model with your original sketchbook for comparison

quest81.title: The Foamsmith's Apprentice
quest81.rationale:
The Foamsmith's Apprentice

Why it's important:
EVA foam is the primary material for modern cosplay construction. This quest teaches the fundamental techniques of cutting, shaping, sealing, and painting foam—skills that directly transfer to armor, weapons, and props. Without mastering these basics, students will struggle with the collaborative cosplay summative.

Skills developed:

  • Safe cutting techniques with hobby knives
  • Heat shaping with heat guns
  • Contact cement application and seam hiding
  • PlastiDip/Komba sealing methods
  • Acrylic painting on flexible surfaces
  • Pattern transfer from 2D to 3D forms

This quest builds the technical foundation required for the Master Forgemaster's Covenant.
quest81.description:
In the workshop of Old Man Kaelen, the kingdom's finest armorsmith has retired to teaching the sacred craft of foam. 'Metal is heavy and unkind,' he grumbles, handing you a sheet of EVA foam. 'But foam... foam can become anything if you learn its secrets.'

Your task is to create basic shapes using EVA foam, demonstrating all five stages of foamsmithing: pattern, cut, shape, seal, and paint.

Demonstrate at least one curved/domed shape achieved through heat forming
Show clean seams with glue (no visible gaps)
Apply proper sealing (PlastiDip, white glue or heat sealing) before painting
Finish with acrylic paint showing base color, shading, and at least one highlight or weathering effect
Write a reflection explaining your process and challenges with each technique
